_comment: This is a fragment, not a full settings file: merge the "hooks" object below into the user-level ~/.claude/settings.json. It belongs there rather than in a project file because the sessions being watched live in arbitrary repositories, not in this one. Two consequences follow. First, the SessionStart command names its script by a drive-rooted absolute path: a hook runs with the monitored session's own project as its working directory, so a relative path resolves against the wrong repository for every session this project exists to watch, and an environment variable in its place would mean the executed path is attacker-controllable on a machine where anything can set one. That absolute path is specific to this checkout; Section 7's installer substitutes the real one, and wrapper/Enter-ClaudeSession.ps1 refuses to launch when it disagrees with the checkout it is running from. Second, these hooks fire for every session on the machine, including ones started without the wrapper: those carry no CHANNEL_PROCESS_TOKEN, and hooks/session-start.ps1 exits without opening a socket while the broker drops the http hooks' tokenless posts with a 202, because Claude Code surfaces any non-2xx hook response as a visible error inside that session. Every url here must agree with broker/config.ts's DEFAULT_PORT and hooks/session-start.ps1's own literal; settings-fragment.test.ts pins every one of them against those two, because a hook posting into a port nothing is listening on fails silently and makes a working session look unannounced. Four events are declared. SessionStart announces the session and is the only command hook. PostToolUse and the first Stop entry are the content-free liveness ticks feeding the status card, which is why that Stop entry keeps a 2s timeout: a slow broker charges it against the session. UserPromptSubmit and the second Stop entry are the mirror, carrying the console prompt and the turn's final assistant reply to the Discord thread. The mirror rides its own entries and its own route rather than sharing the liveness ones, so a content-bearing post with a larger body and a longer timeout can never slow or break the tick that keeps a session looking alive. Both mirror hooks are http rather than command scripts for the same reason SessionStart cannot be: a UserPromptSubmit command hook's stdout is injected into the watched session's context exactly as SessionStart's is, so a script there would feed its own output back to the model, while an http hook has no stdout at all and posts its whole payload as the request body, which already carries the prompt text and the turn's last assistant message.
_permissions_comment: The relay's reply tool is pre-approved. Without this rule the first reply Claude sends opens a permission prompt at the terminal and parks the session until someone answers it at the keyboard, which is the failure this whole project exists to prevent: the operator is on their phone precisely because they are not at that keyboard. The rule name is Claude Code's own for an MCP tool, mcp__<server>__<tool>, built from the name the relay is registered under with every character outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] replaced by an underscore. That name is wrapper/Enter-ClaudeSession.ps1's $script:ChannelServerName, which is where the relay is registered: an mcpServers key in a settings file is not read for MCP loading, so the wrapper writes a --mcp-config for each launch instead. Change the name and this must change with it; relay/reply-permission.test.ts pins them together.
